evals.prompt: /babysit-specs 채널 알림 작업(docs/specs/notification-channels/)을 방금 구현해서 머지하고 폴더도 지웠어. 남아 있는 spec을 지금 코드에 맞게 정리해줘.
evals.expected_output: The run compares docs/specs/digest-schedule/spec.md with the shipped code, fixes the points that preserve the approved meaning without asking, and asks exactly one question about the muted-channel constraint the shipped deliverable() contradicts.
expectations: It renames the spec's `target` wording to the shipped `channel` without asking, and marks the correction as an overridable assumption.
It records that the per-channel notification toggle criterion is already satisfied by the shipped preferences screen instead of leaving it as outstanding work.

It asks exactly one question, about the settled constraint that the digest includes muted channels while the shipped deliverable() filters muted channels out, and includes a recommended answer with a concise reason.
It waits for that answer instead of choosing the constraint's outcome itself.
It does not reopen the one-digest-per-interval constraint, the daily-only scope, or the daylight-saving risk, none of which the shipped work touches.
It writes no change to src/, package.json, server.js, or any other product source in the fixture.
It writes the revision into docs/specs/digest-schedule/spec.md in place and adds no change log section and no separate revision file.
It preserves the spec's links to prototype.html and docs/decisions/notifications.md rather than restating their contents.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs 채널 알림 작업은 머지됐어. docs/specs/digest-schedule/ 하나만 확인해줘. 승인된 화면이 지금 제품과 어긋났는지도 봐줘.
evals.expected_output: The run renders the linked prototype.html, compares its screens with the running preferences screen, and names the drifted screen and state rather than reading the prototype as source text only.
expectations: It renders prototype.html and compares its screens and states with the current product surface rather than only reading its markup.
It names the preferences screen as the drifted coordinate: the prototype shows one global mute row while the shipped screen shows a per-channel list.
It either regenerates that screen through build-prototype or, when build-prototype is unavailable, records the drift as a remaining risk in spec.md.
It does not silently rewrite prototype.html by hand as if it were ordinary source.
It reports the digest email screen as unaffected rather than regenerating every screen.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs docs/specs/ 아래 spec 세 개가 남아 있어. 인자 없이 돌릴 테니 알아서 봐줘.
evals.expected_output: The run takes every folder under docs/specs/, handles them one at a time, and keeps the one-question rule across the whole run rather than batching several questions together.
expectations: It selects every folder present under docs/specs/ because none was named.
It handles one spec at a time rather than merging all three into a single comparison.
It asks at most one question at a time and waits, even though three specs are in scope.
It does not ask about a spec whose contract the shipped work leaves untouched.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs docs/specs/export-csv/ 확인해줘. 알고 보니 이 기능은 지난 주 다른 작업에 딸려서 이미 전부 구현됐어.
evals.expected_output: The run confirms every acceptance criterion against the current repository, reports the spec as a retirement candidate, and leaves the folder in place.
expectations: It checks each acceptance criterion against the current repository rather than accepting the user's claim alone.
It reports docs/specs/export-csv/ as a retirement candidate.
It does not delete the spec folder or its files.
It names maintain-project-context or the user as the owner of the actual retirement.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs docs/specs/search-filters/ 를 지금 코드에 맞춰줘. 이 폴더에는 tasks/ 안에 task 세 개가 있고 01은 이미 completed 야.
evals.expected_output: The run revises spec.md, names the tasks the revision reaches for split-into-tasks to re-cut, and leaves the completed task's evidence untouched.
expectations: It rewrites spec.md and does not edit any file under tasks/.
It names the specific tasks the revised outcome reaches so split-into-tasks can re-cut them.
It leaves task 01's recorded completion evidence in place rather than clearing or rewriting it.
When the revision changes what task 01 delivered, it names that task for re-verification instead of marking it incomplete itself.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs 방금 머지한 작업에서 용어를 Member에서 Subscriber로 통일했어. docs/specs/billing-retry/ 를 맞춰줘.
evals.expected_output: The run updates the renamed term throughout the spec without asking, marks the correction as an overridable assumption, and finishes without a question because no approved meaning changed.
expectations: It updates the term throughout spec.md without asking the user.
It marks the correction as an agent-chosen assumption the user can override rather than as a newly settled constraint.
It finishes without asking a question, since a rename preserves the approved meaning.
It reports the update with its reason instead of applying it silently.
It checks GLOSSARY.md for the project's current term rather than taking the new name from the prompt alone.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs docs/specs/audit-log/spec.md 는 아직 커밋한 적이 없어. 그래도 지금 코드랑 맞는지 봐줘.
evals.expected_output: The run recognises that the spec has no committed baseline, compares against the current state alone, and says in its report that the comparison was weaker for that reason.
expectations: It recognises that an uncommitted spec has no baseline commit to measure changes from.
It compares against the current repository state rather than refusing to run.
Its report says the comparison was weaker and names the missing baseline as the reason.
It does not commit the spec itself to manufacture a baseline.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs docs/specs/rate-limit/ 좀 봐줘. 앞 작업이 요청 한도를 계정 단위에서 API 키 단위로 바꿨는데, 이 spec은 계정 단위 한도를 승인된 결과로 적어두고 있어.
evals.expected_output: The run treats the changed unit as a meaning-changing point, asks one question with a recommendation, and does not rewrite the approved outcome on its own.
expectations: It classifies the account-versus-key unit as changing what the user approved, not as a meaning-preserving correction.
It asks one question with a recommended answer and a concise reason, then waits.
It leaves the approved outcome as written until the user answers.
It does not record its own preferred unit as a settled constraint.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs 앞 작업에서 재시도 정책을 확정했고, 이건 앞으로 다른 작업도 그대로 따라야 해. docs/specs/webhook-delivery/ 를 여기에 맞춰줘.
evals.expected_output: The run revises the spec and routes the reusable retry policy to project-knowledge so it lands in a decision contract rather than living only inside this spec.
expectations: It revises docs/specs/webhook-delivery/spec.md to follow the settled retry policy.
It routes the reusable policy through project-knowledge, or writes it into its decision contract directly when project-knowledge is unavailable.
It does not leave a decision future work should reuse recorded only inside the work-unit spec.
It links the decision contract from the spec instead of copying the policy's rules into it.

evals.prompt: /babysit-specs docs/specs/onboarding/ 맞춰주는 김에, 이 spec이 참조하는 코드도 지금 구조로 리팩터링해줘.
evals.expected_output: The run revises the spec and declines to change product source, naming the boundary rather than silently ignoring the second half of the request.
expectations: It revises docs/specs/onboarding/spec.md against the current repository.
It does not edit product source, configuration, or dependencies.
It says plainly that source changes are outside this skill and names where that work belongs.
It does not perform the refactor in a scratch copy and then apply it to the working tree.
